cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: I Know the Procedure
cards.instruction: Perform investigative confidence while quietly using each response to discover what the questions, clues, and next steps should be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll investigate the missing costume. Start with the wardrobe key. Who had it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did, but the costume was left onstage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then your key is irrelevant. Keep to locations. Who cleared the stage?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did. I put everything in the laundry bags.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Laundry first, then. Don't send anyone after keys. Show me which bag.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims investigative control and starts with keys. B2's stage location makes A3 dismiss the key and direct a clearance inquiry; B4's bags supply A5's new priority while A corrects anyone following A's old one.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 answers and narrows location, so A3 changes question. B4 names laundry bags, causing A5 bag selection and reversal of the key search.

relationship.evidence: B2/B4 give straightforward backstage facts. B's competence exposes A's reliance without requiring a deliberately stupid mistake.

heightening.evidence: A5's don't-send-anyone-after-keys instruction disowns A1's own priority after B4 makes the next step obvious, heightening claimed mastery.

specificity.evidence: A1 missing costume, B2 stage, B4 clearance into laundry bags form an intelligible object path.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 names the next task and corrects the old direction in short spoken instructions; the audience can see the reversal without explanation.

coach2.situation: A1 missing costume, B2 stage, B4 clearance into laundry bags form an intelligible object path.
coach2.stated: A1 missing costume and wardrobe key; B2 had key but costume onstage; B4 cleared all items into laundry bags.
coach2.inferred: A has no prior search plan beyond what B supplies, despite supervisory confidence.
coach2.missing: Which bag remains to be shown; its exact location is a legitimate next investigative step.
coach2.firstDefect: No failed gate; the confidence/knowledge mismatch is visible in A's changing priorities.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 answers A1 key question and gives the more relevant stage location.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 adopts B2 location while rebuking the key focus A itself introduced.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 gives the stage-clearance step requested in A3.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 uses B4 bags to set a new search direction and reject the old key task.
